subject: SIG follow-up: data handling, prompt logs, and training opt-out
messages:

Subject: SIG clarifications: prompt logs / training on customer data

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the SIG. A couple of our reviewers asked for clarifications on the data-handling sections before we can move this to procurement:

1) Do you ever use customer content (including prompts, attachments, or generated responses) to train or improve Redwood models? If yes, please describe opt-in/opt-out mechanisms.

2) How long are prompt logs, debug traces, and KV cache data retained for hosted customers by default? Is that configurable per account or per route?

3) Are prompt logs or debug snapshots accessible to operations or engineering for debugging? If so, what controls/audit trails are in place?

4) We requested a short attestation/statement we can attach to our security review confirming the above for our legal team.

Could you also attach any SOC2/SIG supporting docs or an evidence pack?

Appreciate it — procurement is on a tight timeline.

Best,
Sandeep
Sandeep Rao
Head of Security Operations, CureHealth
procurement@curehealth.com
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SIG clarifications: prompt logs / training on customer data

Hi Sandeep — thanks for the list. Answers below; I attached the SIG answer spreadsheet and our retention policy PDF for auditor reference.

1) Training on customer data
- Redwood does NOT use customer-provided content to train our public or internal model weights by default. We will only include customer data in model training if there is an explicit, documented contractual opt-in (rare; requires engineering controls and review).
- For Dedicated and Private deployments, customers retain full control — there is no data exfiltration to Redwood training pipelines unless explicitly agreed.

2) Retention windows (hosted API)
- Prompt logs / request traces: default retention 30 days for hosted accounts (used for debugging, rate-limit analysis, and abuse detection).
- KV cache: ephemeral and tied to the serving instance; not written to durable customer-facing logs.
- Aggregated telemetry (latency, token counts): retained for 13 months for billing and SLO analytics.
- Retention is configurable at the account level for enterprise customers via the Console — we can shorten to 0 days (no retention) or choose custom windows with a committed configuration for Dedicated contracts.

3) Access, controls, and audit trails
- Engineering/ops access to request logs is gated by role-based access controls (RBAC) and logged in our audit trail.
- Access to raw prompt content is restricted: very limited SRE/ops roles can request temporary, time-bound access for incident debugging; every access requires a ticket and is recorded (who, why, duration).
- We maintain immutable audit logs of each access event and include the ticket id in the log entry.

4) Attestation language (proposed)
- "Redwood Inference attests that customer content is not used to train Redwood models without explicit, contractual opt-in. Prompt logs for hosted customers are retained for 30 days by default and can be configured per account; access to raw prompt material is restricted to a small set of roles, and all access is audited."

Attachments included:
- redwood-retention-policy-2026.pdf (summary of retention windows + configuration instructions)
- sig-answer-sheet-20261203.xlsx (completed SIG data-handling tab)
- kms-diagram.png (high-level key management / envelope encryption)

Links for auditors: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/CureHealth/SIG_evidence_2026 (contains SOC 2 Type II report excerpt, encryption attestations, and the completed SIG).

If you'd like, I can produce a one-paragraph signed attestation on Redwood letterhead for procurement/legal.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
